references.title: Henry E. Kyburg, Probability and the Logic of Rational Belief (1961), Internet Archive record
references.support: The Internet Archive item page confirms the title, 1961 publication date, and access-restricted scan listing. The Kyburg authorship is corroborated by the Penn Online Books catalog record; the original text and argument passage were not accessed, so these records support bibliographic metadata only.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Formal Representations of Belief
references.support: Section 4.2.2 discusses the Lockean threshold, derives the lottery paradox, identifies Kyburg's response of rejecting deductive closure, and describes other approaches that qualify the threshold rule. Secondary reference-work synthesis; it does not establish one resolution as settled.

references.title: Roy Sorensen, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Epistemic Paradoxes
references.support: Sections 3 and 4 explain the lottery argument's agglomeration reasoning, distinguish believing a contradiction from holding jointly inconsistent beliefs, and discuss Kyburg's response; section 4 attributes the preface paradox to Makinson and relates it to Wilder's preface. Secondary reference-work synthesis.

references.title: Gregory Wheeler, A Review of the Lottery Paradox (2007)
references.support: Pages 1–2 lay out the lottery argument and note disagreement over how to diagnose or respond to it, including the comparison with the preface paradox; section 3.1, p. 19, distinguishes issues about statistical evidence and knowledge from rational belief. Scholarly secondary analysis, not treated as a consensus statement.
